messages:
ops-alert-bot: [ALERT] Increased GPU errors detected for /v1/generate. Multiple containers showing restarts and kernel-level CUDA illegal memory access on gpunode-7 and gpunode-8. Sample log:
```
[2026-03-15T18:32:12Z] runtime: cuda: illegal memory access (misaligned address) kernel: pagewalk fault at 0x7ff...
[2026-03-15T18:32:13Z] container: exit code 137, restarting
```

sara: I'm oncall. seeing a big spike in OOMs + CUDA ILLEGAL on gpunode-7,8. Starting triage. Anyone from infra able to join?

ryan: paging in, on it. pulling pod logs now. noticing container restart loop, kernel messages show pagewalk faults and addr misalignment. also seeing recent driver rollout last night.

mike: eng-runtime here. could be driver regression or a kernel/driver interaction with our new KV cache warmup optimization. recommend isolating a node and running a canary rollback of the driver.

lisa: ML side: long-context chat models ramping up KV cache usage early in the session — higher memory pressure. we can temporarily disable prefix caching for heavy sessions while triaging.

sara: mitigation plan (short):
  1) cordon gpunode-7 and drain pods to other nodes
  2) scale down batch workers to 0.5x to reduce memory pressure
  3) route critical customers to CPU-fallback model and dedicated pool to preserve SLAs
  4) attempt driver rollback on a single node as canary / apply kernel hotpatch if available
Applying step 1 now.

ops-deploy-bot: drain started for gpunode-7. evicting pods: 12 (expected disruptions: small window).

ryan: note — draining triggers some 502s while requests rebind. applying traffic smoothing: increase retry backoff and route excess to dedicated pool.

mike: quick canary: restarting container runtime on gpunode-8 with env NV_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1 to test if prefetch interacts with misaligned pagewalks. will monitor.

lisa: canary observed 5 minutes without ILLEGAL on gpunode-8, but throughput dropped ~15%. worth it to protect customers.

sara: customer impact summary: ~48 customers experienced elevated 5xx during the peak window. largest impact tenant is 'Acme Analytics' with ~30% error rate bump and a few timed-out streaming responses. support notified.

support-bot: new ticket created: INC-2026-324 for 'Acme Analytics', severity P2. contacts notified.

ryan: rolling back driver on gpunode-7 to previous stable (530.41) now. doing controlled node reboot after unload. will keep one node as a canary.

ops-alert-bot: gpunode-7 reboot initiated (expected). monitoring node health.

sara: monitoring logs and metrics. if ILLEGAL recurs after rollback we'll escalate to kernel team and open vendor support case.

mike: observed correlation: pagewalk misaligned faults spike when sequence length > 8k and KV cache reuse occurs across segments. creating reproduction steps and local harness. filing an internal bug with stack traces.

lisa: adding eval jobs to nightly CI to run long-context prompt set 'long-context-flush' across quantized models to surface regressions.

sara: oncall handoff scheduled in 50m to ryan. leaving action summary and mitigation notes here.

ryan: acknowledged. current state: gpunode-7 cordoned and rebooting, gpunode-8 has NV_DISABLE_PREFETCH canary running, batch workers scaled down, cpu-fallback routing active. 5xx rate trending down toward baseline. will keep watches for 2h quiet.

ops-incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-324-ILLEGAL-MEM-DRIFT. Postmortem template: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-324.

sara: thanks for the quick responses. removing temporary general fallback route; keeping cpu-fallback for only the most impacted tenants.

mike: follow-ups to track: [1] vendor kernel/driver ticket with reproducer and traces, [2] add memcheck harness for long-context workloads to CI, [3] implement runtime auto-fallback to known-compatible model variant on detected illegal-access patterns.

lisa: I'll run the full model evals overnight and post results in the incident doc.

ryan: handoff to @natalie in 50m for overnight watch.

ops-alert-bot: monitoring still active: 5xx at baseline, pagewalk ILLEGAL flag active.

natalie: picking up handoff, thanks. anything else I should watch for besides the ILLEGAL counts and node reboots? :coffee:

sara: watch eviction rates during drain, retry backoff metrics, and any recurrence on nodes with NV_DISABLE_PREFETCH set. notes saved in incident doc.

ryan: closing loop: observed stability on canary, error rate down to baseline, leaving cordon in place until vendor confirms root cause.

sara: good work team. I'll draft the initial incident notes for the postmortem and assign follow-ups.
